disclaimer: Advisories are decision support, not a prescription. Insecticide and fungicide choice, dose, water volume and pre-harvest interval must follow the product label and the recommendations of the State Agriculture Department / local KVK. Always confirm a high-impact diagnosis with an extension officer before a field-wide spray.

disease.headline: Possible disease detected
steps: Walk a diagonal transect and record how many plants in 100 show the same symptom.
Remove and destroy (do not compost) severely affected leaves and plants.
Avoid overhead irrigation and stop working in the field while the canopy is wet.
ipm: Improve air movement by weeding and correct spacing.
Switch the next irrigation to furrow or drip.
disease.chemical_guidance: Use a protectant fungicide/bactericide approved for this crop-disease pair in your state; rotate the mode-of-action group between sprays.
disease.irrigation_advice: Keep the canopy dry - irrigate early in the day, at the root zone.
disease.escalate_if: More than 10% of plants affected, or the spot count doubles within 48 hours.

pest.headline: Pest activity detected
steps: Count the pest on 3 leaves each from 10 randomly chosen plants and compare with the economic threshold.
Install or check pheromone / yellow sticky traps to confirm the trend.
Treat only the affected patch first - do not spray the whole field on a single detection.
ipm: Conserve natural enemies; avoid broad-spectrum insecticides.
Remove alternate weed hosts on bunds.
pest.chemical_guidance: Spray only after the economic threshold is crossed, using an insecticide approved for this crop-pest pair; rotate chemistry to slow resistance.
pest.irrigation_advice: No irrigation change required for this detection alone.
pest.escalate_if: The economic threshold is crossed, or counts rise on two consecutive scouting rounds.

deficiency.headline: Possible nutrient deficiency
steps: Confirm the pattern - which leaves (old vs new) and whether the veins stay green.
Check the latest soil test; sample again if it is more than one season old.
Correct with a foliar spray for a quick response and adjust the soil dose for the next split.
deficiency.chemical_guidance: Follow the soil-test-based recommendation for the crop; foliar sprays correct symptoms but do not replace the soil dose.
deficiency.irrigation_advice: Keep moisture adequate - nutrient uptake stops in dry soil.
deficiency.escalate_if: Symptoms persist 10-14 days after correction, which suggests a pH or root problem rather than supply.

abiotic.headline: Crop stress detected
steps: Check soil moisture at root depth before acting.
Compare with the weather forecast for the next 48 hours.
abiotic.chemical_guidance: No plant protection product is indicated for abiotic stress.
abiotic.irrigation_advice: Adjust the irrigation schedule as advised below.
abiotic.escalate_if: Symptoms persist after the root zone is at field capacity.

healthy.headline: Crop looks healthy
steps: Continue the normal scouting round.
healthy.escalate_if: Any new spotting, curling or discolouration appears.

background.headline: No crop leaf in the picture
steps: Hold the camera 20-30 cm from a single leaf, fill the frame, and avoid direct shadow.

tomato__late_blight.headline: Late blight suspected - act today
tomato__late_blight.farmer_message: Late blight suspected on tomato. It can destroy the field in 3-5 days of cool wet weather. Remove affected plants and apply a protectant spray today.
steps: Uproot and bury or burn badly affected plants NOW - do not leave them on the bund.
Apply a protectant fungicide the same day, covering the underside of the leaves.
Stop overhead irrigation completely until the weather dries.
Warn neighbouring farmers - blight spreads field to field on the wind.
ipm: Destroy volunteer potato/tomato plants nearby.
Widen spacing at the next planting and use resistant varieties.
tomato__late_blight.chemical_guidance: A protectant (contact) fungicide first, followed by a systemic from a different mode-of-action group if wet weather continues. Confirm the product and dose with your KVK.
tomato__late_blight.irrigation_advice: Suspend overhead irrigation; irrigate in furrows early in the morning only.
tomato__late_blight.escalate_if: New lesions appear on upper leaves within 24 hours.

potato__late_blight.headline: Late blight suspected - act today
potato__late_blight.farmer_message: Late blight suspected on potato. Spray a protectant today and stop overhead irrigation - the crop can be lost within a week in cool humid weather.
steps: Apply a protectant fungicide today with full underside coverage.
Remove and destroy affected haulm; do not dump it at the field edge.
Plan to dehaulm 2-3 weeks before harvest to protect the tubers.
Do not irrigate overhead while humidity stays above 85%.
ipm: Earth up well so spores cannot reach the tubers.
Use certified disease-free seed tubers next season.
potato__late_blight.chemical_guidance: Protectant contact fungicide first; alternate mode-of-action groups if the wet spell continues. Confirm dose with your KVK.
potato__late_blight.irrigation_advice: Suspend irrigation during the wet spell; resume light furrow irrigation once the canopy dries.
potato__late_blight.escalate_if: Lesions spread to stems, or more than 5% of the canopy is affected.

rice__blast.headline: Rice blast suspected
rice__blast.farmer_message: Rice blast suspected. Stop any further nitrogen top-dressing and treat before the panicle stage - neck blast can empty the grain.
steps: Stop nitrogen top-dressing immediately - excess N drives blast.
Drain and re-flood the field to break the humid micro-climate.
Treat at boot-leaf stage to protect the neck if lesions are on the flag leaf.
ipm: Balance N with potash and silicon.
Choose blast-resistant varieties next season and treat the seed.
rice__blast.chemical_guidance: A systemic fungicide recommended for blast in your state, applied at the boot stage; confirm with the KVK.
rice__blast.irrigation_advice: Alternate wetting and drying rather than continuous deep flooding.
rice__blast.escalate_if: Lesions reach the flag leaf or the neck of emerging panicles.

rice__bacterial_leaf_blight.headline: Bacterial leaf blight suspected
rice__bacterial_leaf_blight.farmer_message: Bacterial leaf blight suspected. Fungicides do not work on this. Drain the field, stop nitrogen, and avoid moving through the wet crop.
steps: Drain the standing water for 2-3 days where the crop stage allows.
Stop nitrogen top-dressing until the spread stops.
Do not walk through the wet crop - the bacteria spread on leaves and tools.
ipm: Avoid clipping seedling tips at transplanting.
Use resistant varieties and clean seed next season.
rice__bacterial_leaf_blight.chemical_guidance: This is bacterial - ordinary fungicides are ineffective. Use only a bactericide approved in your state, if any is recommended.
rice__bacterial_leaf_blight.irrigation_advice: Drain; keep shallow water rather than deep flooding.
rice__bacterial_leaf_blight.escalate_if: Wilting of whole seedlings (kresek) appears, or more than 20% leaf area is affected.

tomato__yellow_leaf_curl_virus.headline: Leaf curl virus suspected - control whitefly
tomato__yellow_leaf_curl_virus.farmer_message: Tomato leaf curl virus suspected. There is no cure for the virus - remove infected plants and control whitefly at once to stop it spreading.
steps: Uproot and destroy infected plants - they will not recover and act as a source.
Control whitefly immediately; the virus spreads only through the vector.
Install yellow sticky traps at 10-12 per acre just above the canopy.
Remove parthenium and other weed hosts on the bunds.
ipm: Use a border crop of maize/sorghum as a barrier.
Raise nurseries under 40-mesh insect-proof net.
Prefer tolerant hybrids next season.
tomato__yellow_leaf_curl_virus.chemical_guidance: Target the whitefly vector, rotating insecticide groups. No product cures the virus itself.
tomato__yellow_leaf_curl_virus.irrigation_advice: Maintain even moisture; stressed plants show worse symptoms.
tomato__yellow_leaf_curl_virus.escalate_if: More than 10% of plants show curling, or whitefly counts keep rising.

cotton__leaf_curl_virus.headline: Cotton leaf curl virus suspected
cotton__leaf_curl_virus.farmer_message: Cotton leaf curl suspected. Remove infected plants and bring whitefly under control now - the virus has no cure.
steps: Rogue out infected plants early in the season.
Bring whitefly below threshold; that is the only way to stop spread.
Destroy alternate hosts (bhindi, weeds) around the field.
ipm: Avoid excessive nitrogen, which favours whitefly.
Sow recommended tolerant varieties at the recommended date.
cotton__leaf_curl_virus.chemical_guidance: Vector management only, rotating insecticide groups; consult your KVK for the current state advisory.
cotton__leaf_curl_virus.irrigation_advice: Avoid moisture stress, which worsens symptom expression.
cotton__leaf_curl_virus.escalate_if: Incidence crosses 10% of plants, or new flushes emerge already curled.

sugarcane__red_rot.headline: Red rot suspected - do not use this cane as seed
sugarcane__red_rot.farmer_message: Red rot suspected in sugarcane. Split a drying cane to confirm the red tissue with white patches. Remove affected clumps with roots and never use this field's cane as seed.
steps: Split a drying cane lengthwise and check for red tissue crossed by white patches.
Uproot affected clumps along with roots and burn them.
Do not take seed cane from this field.
Stop irrigation flowing from the affected patch to healthy areas.
ipm: Plant only resistant varieties and heat/fungicide-treated setts.
Rotate with rice or a non-host crop for 2 seasons.
sugarcane__red_rot.chemical_guidance: There is no effective standing-crop cure. Management is varietal resistance, sett treatment and sanitation.
sugarcane__red_rot.irrigation_advice: Improve drainage; avoid water flowing from infected to healthy patches.
sugarcane__red_rot.escalate_if: More than 5% clumps affected - plan a variety change for the next planting.

grape__downy_mildew.headline: Downy mildew suspected - protect before the next rain
grape__downy_mildew.farmer_message: Downy mildew suspected on grape. Spray a protectant before the next rain or dew and improve canopy air movement.
steps: Apply a protectant cover spray before the next expected rain or heavy dew.
Remove affected leaves and open up the canopy for airflow.
Avoid evening irrigation that leaves the canopy wet overnight.
ipm: Manage canopy density and shoot positioning.
Track leaf wetness hours - infection needs a wet period.
grape__downy_mildew.chemical_guidance: Protectant before rain, systemic curative only within the recommended window; rotate groups and respect residue limits for export.
grape__downy_mildew.irrigation_advice: Irrigate at the root zone in the morning; never wet the canopy in the evening.
grape__downy_mildew.escalate_if: Oil spots appear on more than 5% of leaves or on the bunches.

pest__fall_armyworm.headline: Fall armyworm detected
pest__fall_armyworm.farmer_message: Fall armyworm detected in maize. Check 10 plants for whorl damage. If 5 or more in 100 are damaged, treat the whorl of affected plants only - not the whole field.
steps: Count damaged whorls in 100 plants to get the infestation percentage.
Hand-pick and crush egg masses and large larvae in a small field.
Apply into the WHORL of affected plants only - the larva sits inside, blanket spraying wastes chemical.
Place 5 pheromone traps per acre to track moth flight.
ipm: Deep summer ploughing to expose pupae.
Release Trichogramma cards where locally available.
Apply dry sand + ash into the whorl as a low-cost first response in small plots.
Intercrop with pulses and keep field borders weed-free.
pest__fall_armyworm.chemical_guidance: Only above the 5-10% whorl damage threshold, with a whorl-directed application of an approved insecticide; rotate groups every application.
pest__fall_armyworm.irrigation_advice: No change needed for the pest itself.
pest__fall_armyworm.escalate_if: Damage crosses 10% of plants, or larvae reach the tassel/cob stage.

pest__brown_planthopper.headline: Brown planthopper - hopper burn risk
pest__brown_planthopper.farmer_message: Brown planthopper detected in rice. Part the hills and count at the base. Drain the field for 3-4 days and stop nitrogen. Circular dried patches mean hopper burn is starting.
steps: Part the canopy and count hoppers at the base of 20 hills, just above the water line.
Drain the field for 3-4 days - this alone knocks the population back.
Stop nitrogen top-dressing.
If spraying, direct the nozzle at the BASE of the plants, not the canopy top.
ipm: Never use a broad-spectrum insecticide - it kills spiders and mirid bugs and causes resurgence.
Keep 30 cm alleys every 2-3 m for aeration and spray access.
Avoid dense planting and excess nitrogen.
pest__brown_planthopper.chemical_guidance: Only above 10 hoppers/hill (pre-flowering) with natural enemies absent; use a selective insecticide directed at the plant base.
pest__brown_planthopper.irrigation_advice: Drain for 3-4 days, then keep shallow intermittent water.
pest__brown_planthopper.escalate_if: Circular yellow-brown patches (hopper burn) appear anywhere in the field - treat as an emergency.

pest__whitefly.headline: Whitefly detected - virus vector
pest__whitefly.farmer_message: Whitefly detected. Besides sucking sap it spreads leaf curl virus. Put up yellow sticky traps and check the underside of the top 3 leaves.
steps: Count adults on the underside of the top 3 leaves of 10 plants in the early morning.
Install yellow sticky traps at 10-12 per acre just above the canopy.
Remove and destroy weed hosts on the bunds.
ipm: Spray neem oil covering leaf undersides.
Avoid excess nitrogen.
Conserve Encarsia and predatory beetles by avoiding broad-spectrum sprays.
pest__whitefly.chemical_guidance: Above 6 adults/leaf, use an approved insecticide with good underside coverage; rotate groups strictly - whitefly develops resistance fast.
pest__whitefly.irrigation_advice: No change needed for the pest itself.
pest__whitefly.escalate_if: Counts rise for two consecutive scouting rounds, or leaf-curl symptoms start appearing.

pest__pink_bollworm.headline: Pink bollworm detected
pest__pink_bollworm.farmer_message: Pink bollworm detected in cotton. Open 20 green bolls to check for pink larvae and count rosette flowers. Destroy affected material and never extend the crop beyond the recommended season.
steps: Open 20 green bolls from across the field and record how many have larvae.
Collect and destroy rosetted flowers and damaged bolls.
Install 2 pheromone traps per acre and count moths nightly.
Terminate the crop on time - carry-over crops build the next season's population.
ipm: Release Trichogramma bactrae where available.
Do not ratoon cotton.
Deep ploughing after harvest to destroy carry-over larvae.
pest__pink_bollworm.chemical_guidance: Only after 8 moths/trap/night for 3 nights or 10% rosette flowers; rotate insecticide groups every spray.
pest__pink_bollworm.irrigation_advice: Avoid late irrigation that extends the crop past its recommended duration.
pest__pink_bollworm.escalate_if: More than 10% of opened bolls contain larvae.

pest__spider_mite.headline: Spider mite infestation
pest__spider_mite.farmer_message: Spider mites detected. They multiply in hot dry weather and after broad-spectrum sprays. Do not use a normal insecticide - it makes mites worse.
steps: Check leaf undersides with a hand lens for mites and fine webbing.
Wash the canopy with a strong water spray in a small plot.
Treat the affected patch with a specific miticide, covering leaf undersides.
ipm: Stop broad-spectrum insecticides - they kill predatory mites and cause flare-ups.
Keep the crop free of moisture stress.
Control dust on field roads.
pest__spider_mite.chemical_guidance: Use a specific acaricide, not a general insecticide, and alternate the group between applications.
pest__spider_mite.irrigation_advice: Avoid moisture stress - dry stressed plants favour mites.
pest__spider_mite.escalate_if: Webbing spreads across the upper canopy or bronzing covers more than 10% of leaf area.

deficiency__nitrogen.headline: Nitrogen deficiency likely
deficiency__nitrogen.farmer_message: Older leaves yellowing from the bottom up suggests nitrogen shortage. Apply a split top-dress with enough soil moisture, and use a leaf colour chart before the next dose.
steps: Confirm that the yellowing starts on the OLDEST leaves - new-leaf yellowing means a different nutrient.
Apply the nitrogen top-dress as a split dose with adequate soil moisture.
Use a leaf colour chart (LCC) to time the next split in rice.
deficiency__nitrogen.chemical_guidance: Follow the soil-test based split schedule. Excess nitrogen invites blast, BLB, planthopper and whitefly - do not overdose.
deficiency__nitrogen.irrigation_advice: Irrigate lightly after top-dressing so the nutrient reaches the root zone.
deficiency__nitrogen.escalate_if: No greening within 10-14 days - check for waterlogging or root damage.

deficiency__zinc.headline: Zinc deficiency likely
deficiency__zinc.farmer_message: Zinc deficiency (khaira) likely - rusty brown patches on the middle leaves with stunting. A foliar zinc spray gives the quickest response; correct the soil dose next season.
steps: Confirm the rusty-brown interveinal blotching on middle leaves with shortened internodes.
Apply a foliar zinc sulphate spray, neutralised as recommended for your crop.
Repeat after 10-15 days if symptoms persist.
deficiency__zinc.chemical_guidance: Soil application of zinc sulphate at the recommended rate every 2-3 seasons; foliar spray for immediate correction.
deficiency__zinc.irrigation_advice: Drain waterlogged patches - continuous flooding worsens zinc deficiency in rice.
deficiency__zinc.escalate_if: Symptoms persist after two foliar sprays - test the soil pH.

abiotic__water_stress.headline: Water stress - irrigate
abiotic__water_stress.farmer_message: Crop shows water stress (leaf rolling, dull canopy). Check soil moisture at root depth and irrigate if the sensor is below the set point.
steps: Confirm with the soil moisture sensor at root depth before irrigating.
If leaves stay rolled after 9-10 am, irrigate the same day.
Irrigate early morning or evening to cut evaporation loss.
abiotic__water_stress.chemical_guidance: No plant protection product is indicated.
abiotic__water_stress.irrigation_advice: Irrigate now if soil moisture is below the crop set point; prefer drip or alternate-furrow to save water.
abiotic__water_stress.escalate_if: Rolling continues 24 hours after irrigation - check for root disease, nematodes or a hardpan.

abiotic__heat_scald.headline: Heat stress warning
abiotic__heat_scald.farmer_message: Heat stress damage visible. Give a light irrigation in the evening, and avoid spraying or fertiliser application during the hot hours.
steps: Give a light irrigation in the late evening or early morning to cool the root zone.
Do not spray during peak heat - it scorches the leaf and wastes chemical.
Mulch the root zone where possible.
abiotic__heat_scald.chemical_guidance: No plant protection product is indicated; potassium nutrition improves heat tolerance.
abiotic__heat_scald.irrigation_advice: Shorter, more frequent irrigations during the heat spell; irrigate outside 11:00-16:00.
abiotic__heat_scald.escalate_if: Flower or fruit drop begins, or the forecast holds above 38 C for 3 more days.

abiotic__waterlogging.headline: Waterlogging / flood damage
abiotic__waterlogging.farmer_message: Waterlogging damage detected. Drain standing water as fast as possible - roots suffocate within 2-3 days. Do not apply fertiliser to a flooded field.
steps: Open drainage channels and remove standing water immediately.
Once drained, wash silt off the leaves so the crop can photosynthesise.
Wait for the soil to drain before any fertiliser - it will only leach away.
Watch for root rot and stem rot in the following week.
ipm: Expect a rise in fungal root diseases after flooding - scout in 5-7 days.
abiotic__waterlogging.chemical_guidance: A protective fungicide drench may be advised after prolonged flooding; confirm with your KVK.
abiotic__waterlogging.irrigation_advice: Stop all irrigation; the priority is drainage.
abiotic__waterlogging.escalate_if: Water stands for more than 48 hours, or plants wilt after the water recedes.
